newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico putting more port assets on the block.
newsitem.headline: Mexico putting more port assets on the block.

text.p: Mexico is preparing to privatize administration and towing services at a number of ports in coming months, port administration coordinator Eduardo Aspero said.

The government recently announced it will auction towing rights at Veracruz port, a key grains, auto parts and container shipping site. Interested participants must register for the bidding by June 27 with a decision due on Oct. 17.
The winning bidder will offer towing services alongside a current private provider in Veracruz in 1995, Aspero told Reuters in a phone interview late Tuesday.
The Philippines' ICTSI and Mexican builder Empresas ICA SA won rights to the container terminal at Veracruz.
In July Mexico plans to open the bidding for the administration of Puerto Vallarta, mostly a tourist port.

The following month, bidding will begin for towing services at Ensenada, Mazatlan, Guaymas and Altamira ports, Aspero said. At least 10 companies, many of them foreign-owned, have expressed interest so far in the biddings, he added.

Operations at the multiple-use terminal at Manzanillo and the container terminal at Lazaro Cardenas will begin privatization in September, Aspero said. He said mostly Mexican companies have expressed interest in operating the terminals.

In March Mexico sold 20-year operating rights for the port of Ensenada to ICTSI as part of a continuing process to privatize the nation's ports. Mexico's largest transportation company, Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM), won a tugboat concession for Manzanillo in December.
